result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives exact point sizes for five clear levels, sets dish names apart with semibold, and aligns prices on a shared decimal tab using tabular figures. It also letterspaces the capitals and keeps the footer at a firm 9 pt minimum. Answer B is solid but gives size ranges, sets dish names at the same size as the section heads, and centres the prices instead of aligning them. Its footer may be too small and grey to read easily, and it adds more options and effects such as a second typeface, ornaments and an accent colour. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives exact point sizes, spacing and leading for each level. It aligns prices on a shared decimal tab with tabular figures, sets letterspacing on the caps headings and keeps the footer at a legible 9 pt minimum. A is solid on hierarchy and spacing, but its price advice contradicts itself (drop decimals vs. use .50) and gives no consistent alignment edge. A's grey 8.5 pt footer also risks being hard to read.
